named_confounds: genre composition shift (juvenile share rises, historical/domestic_realist shares fall after 1876)
small early-period cells (37-165 works per genre before 1876)
single passage per work (n_passages=1) limits within-work precision
rationale: Data: 6766 works, one coded passage each, years 1800s-1920s; 752 works before 1876 and 6014 from 1876 on. Outcome is count__domains__DISTANCE_TRAVEL / n_passages. Estimand: work rates averaged with equal weight inside each genre x period cell, then the late-minus-early difference averaged with equal weight across the 8 genres, giving +0.052. The 95% CI [0.034, 0.069] comes from a 1000-replicate bootstrap that resamples works within each genre x period cell. All 8 genres go up, by roughly 0.04 to 0.06 each. Decade means also rise, from about 0.04-0.07 before 1880 to about 0.11-0.12 from 1890 on. Artifact checks: the genre mix does change across the cutoff (juvenile goes from 21% to 34% of works, historical from 22% to 10%). Because the estimand is computed within genres, this change does not drive the result. Origin, date_confidence, mean n_editions (1.08 in both periods) and author productivity are almost the same in both periods. Stratified estimates hold up: high/medium/low date confidence give 0.049/0.055/0.045, and UK/US/unknown origin give 0.039/0.032/0.064. An OLS model adjusting for genre, origin, date_confidence, log editions and log author productivity, with SEs clustered by author, gives 0.051 [0.033, 0.070]. Caveats: the early cells are small; some early genre cells have a rate of zero (domestic_realist, romance); the domain codes come from a classifier and may be measured differently across periods; and the corpus may have been sampled differently in different periods. The cited passages are late-period passages coded with this domain. They show what the construct looks like but cannot by themselves establish the trend.
